html:
Juraj Jánošík was a Slovak highwayman, born in 1688 in Terchová in northern Slovakia and executed at Liptovský Mikuláš in 1713. Legend made him a Robin Hood who robbed lords and gave to the poor.

He fought as a young man in the Rákóczi uprising against the Habsburgs, then served as a prison guard and joined an outlaw band whose leader he soon became. He was caught, tried and, the story goes, hung by his ribs from a hook. Songs and tales spread his fame across the Carpathians, and the poets of the Štúr generation made him a national symbol. Films and plays about him are still made in Slovakia and Poland.
